item_name: LANDING PATTERN (NORMAL, NO FLAP, FLAP T/O - AΟA)

observations.text: SP flew the normal overhead pattern to the desired standard for this Training Section, with the IP directing the break point and calling the gear and flap selections. Break altitude deviated by up to 380 feet, the downwind airspeed decayed 12 knots below the pattern airspeed, and the IP executed part of the turn to final. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent sequencing of the break, the required checks and the standardized reports is expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP flew the pattern from the break to the RWY threshold without the IP directing or executing any part of it, requiring verbal indications for the landing checks and for the Roll Out Point. Break altitude was contained within 300 feet with 15 degrees of bank deviation, downwind airspeed reached 20 knots above the pattern airspeed and final altitude stayed within 200 feet high and 100 feet low. Alignment with the RWY centerline was completed at the 1/2 NM point and every deviation was corrected, with delay, after the IP's verbal indications. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern without any prompting from the IP, breaking within the break zone with ATC clearance and after clearing the downwind. Break altitude deviated 250 feet with 13 degrees of bank error, downwind airspeed reached 16 knots above the pattern airspeed and final altitude 150 feet high. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, with the required checks performed and the standardized reports given. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern accurately and promptly, holding break and downwind altitude within 120 feet, break bank within 8 degrees and the downwind airspeed within 7 knots above the pattern airspeed and never below 120 KIAS. The base leg was flown at 40 degrees of bank to the planned Roll Out Point, final altitude was held within 90 feet high and 40 feet low, and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline 3/4 NM prior to the threshold. The required checks were performed within the gear and flap limitations and the standardized reports were given at the correct points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with break altitude and bank deviations of 40 feet and 2 degrees and with the downwind, base leg and final airspeed held within 3 knots of the pattern values. The final was flown without deviation or convergence, the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline well before the 1/2 NM point and no onset of stall characteristics occurred at any point. Drift correction on the base leg was applied in advance, so that the Roll Out Point required no adjustment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a late power reduction after the break, did not place the A/C in the downwind at the pattern altitude and airspeed, rolling out 390 feet high and 26 knots fast. The base turn was started beyond the planned Roll Out Point and the final was flown converging on the RWY centerline, with the result that the IP directed the corrections and executed part of the turn to final. The landing gear was selected only after the IP's call.

SP completed the normal overhead pattern within the desired standards, with break altitude at the 300 feet deviation limit, downwind airspeed 20 knots above the pattern airspeed and final altitude 200 feet high. The gear and flap selections and two standardized reports were made only after the IP's verbal indications, and the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier self-recognition of the altitude and airspeed deviations in the pattern is expected in the following sorties.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern without any verbal prompting from the IP, executing the break within the break zone after clearing the downwind and giving all the standardized reports. Break altitude deviated 230 feet with 12 degrees of bank error, downwind airspeed reached 15 knots above the pattern airspeed and final altitude 140 feet high. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern accurately and promptly, containing break and downwind altitude within 130 feet, break bank within 9 degrees and the downwind and base leg airspeed within 8 knots above the pattern values. The base leg was flown at 42 degrees of bank to the Roll Out Point described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the final was held within 100 feet high and 45 feet low without deviating or converging. The required checks were performed within the gear and flap limitations and the standardized reports were given at the correct points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern with exceptional precision, holding break altitude within 40 feet, break bank within 3 degrees and the downwind, base leg and final airspeed within 4 knots of the pattern values. Alignment with the RWY centerline was established 1 NM prior to the threshold and maintained without deviation or convergence, with final altitude deviations not exceeding 30 feet. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed without any prompting and the drift correction was anticipated on every leg. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the required checks before the base leg and did not maintain the downwind pattern altitude and airspeed, descending 370 feet low and decelerating below 120 KIAS. The base turn was then flown at 50 degrees of bank in an attempt to reach the RWY centerline, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls and directed the go around. The onset of stall characteristics in the base turn was not recognized by the SP.

SP, due to an incorrect drift correction technique on the downwind, did not hold the pattern ground track and displaced the base turn, reaching the final 200 feet high and 15 knots above the final airspeed. Alignment with the RWY centerline was completed at the 1/2 NM point only after the IP's verbal indications, and break altitude had already deviated to the 300 feet limit. The corrections were made with delay and the standardized report on final was given late.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern within the desired standards, with break altitude deviations up to 280 feet, downwind airspeed 18 knots above the pattern airspeed and final altitude 180 feet high. The deviations were recognized and corrected without the IP's intervention, but the corrections were repeated on each leg and the Roll Out Point required two adjustments. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more consistent power and pitch technique on the downwind and base leg is expected to reduce these deviations in the following sorties.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern accurately and promptly, breaking within the break zone with ATC clearance and holding break altitude within 110 feet and break bank within 7 degrees. Downwind altitude was contained within 130 feet with the airspeed within 8 knots above the pattern value and never below 120 KIAS, and final altitude was held within 90 feet high and 40 feet low. The required checks, the gear and flap limitations and the standardized reports were all complied with, and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline before the 1/2 NM point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with break altitude and bank deviations of 35 feet and 2 degrees and with the downwind, base leg and final airspeed held within 3 knots of the pattern values. The base leg was planned so that the roll out occurred on the RWY centerline with final altitude deviations of 25 feet and with no deviation or convergence thereafter. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed early on each leg, leaving the scan free for the traffic and the ATC instructions. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect break technique, did not execute the break within the break zone and did not control the bank and the altitude, exceeding the break altitude by 400 feet with 20 degrees of bank error. The downwind was entered without the required checks, with the result that the IP directed the gear and flap selections and executed the correction to the pattern altitude. The A/C was placed in the downwind below 120 KIAS and the recovery of the airspeed was made by the IP.

SP, due to failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not maintain the final airspeed and altitude after the landing flaps were selected, reaching the 15 knots and 200 feet high limits of the criteria. The deviation from the final was recognized only after the IP's verbal indications and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline at the 1/2 NM point. The corrections were completed without the IP touching the controls, but with delay on both parameters.

SP, due to a late roll out from the base turn, did not plan the final at the Roll Out Point described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, converging on the RWY centerline with 180 feet of altitude deviation and 16 knots above the pattern airspeed. Break altitude deviated 240 feet with 13 degrees of bank error. The errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention and the alignment was completed before the 1/2 NM point.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern within the desired standards, holding break and downwind altitude within 145 feet, break bank within 10 degrees and the final airspeed within 10 knots above the pattern value. The parameters were accurate and the reports were standardized, but the corrections on the base leg were repeated and the final was reached at the outer edge of the criteria on two of the three patterns. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the base leg planning across consecutive patterns is expected to improve.

SP flew the normal overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with break altitude deviations not exceeding 40 feet, break bank within 3 degrees and the downwind, base leg and final airspeed held within 3 knots of the pattern values. Every pattern was flown to the same standard, with the A/C aligned with the RWY centerline 1 NM prior to the threshold and with final altitude deviations of 30 feet. The required checks, the gear and flap limitations and the standardized reports were complied with without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern to the desired standard for this Training Section, with the IP directing the wider downwind spacing and the extended base leg required with the flaps up. Downwind airspeed decayed 14 knots below the no flap pattern airspeed and final altitude reached 140 feet low, with the IP calling the corrections and executing part of the turn to final. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent adjustment of the pattern geometry and of the higher no flap airspeeds is expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP flew the complete no flap overhead pattern without the IP directing or executing any part of it, requiring verbal indications for the extended base leg and for the final airspeed. Downwind altitude deviated to the 300 feet limit, downwind airspeed reached 20 knots above the no flap pattern airspeed and final altitude 200 feet high. The A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline at the 1/2 NM point and the corrections were made with delay after the IP's indications. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern without any prompting from the IP, keeping the flaps up throughout and adhering to the landing gear limitations. Break altitude deviated 260 feet with 12 degrees of bank error, downwind airspeed reached 17 knots above the no flap pattern airspeed and final altitude 160 feet high. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern accurately and promptly, widening the downwind and extending the base leg as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual for the flaps up configuration. Break and downwind altitude were held within 130 feet, the downwind and base leg airspeed within 9 knots above the no flap pattern values and final altitude within 100 feet high and 45 feet low. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline before the 1/2 NM point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern with exceptional precision, holding the higher no flap airspeeds within 3 knots on the downwind, base leg and final and the pattern altitude within 40 feet. The base turn was planned so that the roll out occurred on the RWY centerline with a shallower final flown without deviation or convergence, and no onset of stall characteristics appeared at any point. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed early on each leg without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to retention of the normal pattern mental model after the no flap configuration had been set, did not widen the downwind or extend the base leg and flew the pattern at the normal pattern airspeeds. Final was reached 260 feet high and 22 knots below the no flap final airspeed, with the result that the IP directed the go around and executed part of the correction. The onset of stall characteristics in the base turn was not recognized before the IP's intervention.

SP completed the no flap overhead pattern within the desired standards, with downwind altitude at the 300 feet deviation limit, the base leg airspeed 20 knots above the no flap pattern airspeed and final altitude 200 feet high. The extension of the base leg and one standardized report were made only after the IP's verbal indications and the corrections were applied with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the shallower approach angle required with the flaps up is expected in the following sorties.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern without any verbal prompting from the IP, keeping the flaps up, respecting the landing gear limitations and giving all the standardized reports. Downwind airspeed reached 15 knots above the no flap pattern airspeed, break altitude deviated 220 feet and final altitude 150 feet high. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern accurately and promptly, holding break and downwind altitude within 140 feet, break bank within 9 degrees and the downwind and base leg airspeed within 9 knots above the no flap pattern values. The base leg was extended and flown at 40 degrees of bank to a Roll Out Point that produced a final with altitude deviations within 90 feet high and 40 feet low. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed and there was no deviation or convergence from the final. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with pattern altitude deviations not exceeding 35 feet and with the no flap airspeeds on the downwind, base leg and final held within 3 knots. Alignment with the RWY centerline was established 1 NM prior to the threshold and the shallower no flap final was flown without deviation or convergence. The required checks were performed within the landing gear limitations and the standardized reports were given at the correct points without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect power management technique with the flaps up, did not maintain the no flap final airspeed and allowed the A/C to decelerate 24 knots below it while 320 feet high on the final. The high and slow final produced the onset of stall characteristics, with the result that the IP took the controls and executed the go around. The deviation was not recognized by the SP before the IP's intervention.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in calling for the go around, did not terminate an approach that had reached the 200 feet high and 15 knots fast limits of the final criteria with the flaps up. The A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline only at the 1/2 NM point and the corrections were applied after the IP's verbal indications, with delayed recognition on both parameters. The pattern was completed without the IP touching the controls.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern within the desired standards, with downwind airspeed 17 knots above the no flap pattern airspeed, break altitude deviations of 270 feet and final altitude 170 feet high. The deviations were recognized and corrected without the IP's intervention, but the base leg was extended late on two patterns and the final required a repeated power correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more consistent base leg extension for the flaps up configuration is expected to reduce these corrections.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern accurately and promptly, breaking within the break zone with ATC clearance and holding break altitude within 120 feet and break bank within 8 degrees. The downwind was flown wider with the airspeed within 8 knots above the no flap pattern value, and final altitude was held within 95 feet high and 40 feet low with no deviation or convergence. The required checks were completed within the landing gear limitations and every standardized report was given at the correct point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern with exceptional precision, holding the no flap pattern airspeeds within 3 knots and the break, downwind and final altitudes within 35 feet. The shallower no flap approach angle was anticipated from the base turn, so that the roll out occurred on the RWY centerline and no power correction was required on final. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed early on each leg and no onset of stall characteristics occurred. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a decision error in selecting the normal pattern geometry with the flaps up, did not adapt the downwind spacing or the base leg to the no flap configuration and arrived at the Roll Out Point inside the RWY centerline. The final was flown converging, 350 feet high and 26 knots above the no flap final airspeed, with the result that the IP directed the go around and executed part of the correction. The required checks were completed only after the IP called them.

SP, due to an incorrect pitch and power technique on the base leg, did not maintain the base leg airspeed with the flaps up, reaching the 20 knots limit above the no flap pattern airspeed and arriving on final at the 200 feet high limit. Alignment with the RWY centerline was completed at the 1/2 NM point and the corrections were applied only after the IP's verbal indications. Recognition of both deviations was delayed, but no intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to failure to break the error chain at the first recognizable deviation, did not correct a 12 degree bank error at the break before it produced a downwind 240 feet high and 16 knots above the no flap pattern airspeed. The base leg extension was then late and the final was reached 170 feet high, with the result that two successive corrections were required to regain the RWY centerline. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern within the desired standards, holding break and downwind altitude within 145 feet and the no flap airspeeds within 10 knots above the pattern values. The pattern was accurate and the reports were standardized, but the base leg extension was judged late on one of the three patterns and the final was reached at the outer edge of the altitude criteria. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the flaps up pattern geometry across consecutive patterns is expected to improve.

SP flew the no flap overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with altitude deviations not exceeding 40 feet at the break, on the downwind and on the final and with the no flap airspeeds held within 3 knots. Every pattern was flown to the same geometry, with the roll out on the RWY centerline 1 NM prior to the threshold and with no deviation or convergence on final. The required checks, the landing gear limitations and the standardized reports were complied with without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern to the desired standard for this Training Section, with the IP directing the flap selection to TAKEOFF and the associated airspeed adjustment. Downwind airspeed decayed 13 knots below the pattern airspeed and final altitude reached 250 feet high, with the IP calling the corrections and executing part of the turn to final. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent management of the T/O flap configuration and of its pattern airspeeds is expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP flew the complete flaps T/O overhead pattern without the IP directing or executing any part of it, requiring verbal indications for the flap selection and for the final airspeed. Break altitude deviated to the 300 feet limit with 15 degrees of bank error, and the final was reached 200 feet high and 15 knots fast. Alignment with the RWY centerline was completed at the 1/2 NM point and the corrections followed the IP's verbal indications with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern without any prompting from the IP, selecting the TAKEOFF flap setting within the flap limitation airspeed and completing the required checks. Downwind altitude deviated 240 feet with the airspeed 16 knots above the pattern value, and final altitude reached 150 feet high. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern accurately and promptly, holding break and downwind altitude within 120 feet, break bank within 8 degrees and the downwind and base leg airspeed within 8 knots above the pattern values. The TAKEOFF flap setting and the landing gear were selected within their limitations, the base leg was flown at 40 degrees of bank to the planned Roll Out Point and final altitude was held within 90 feet high and 40 feet low. The standardized reports were given at the correct points and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline before the 1/2 NM point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with break altitude and bank deviations of 35 feet and 2 degrees and with the downwind, base leg and final airspeed held within 3 knots of the T/O flap pattern values. The final was flown without deviation or convergence, with altitude deviations of 25 feet and with no onset of stall characteristics. The configuration change, the required checks and the standardized reports were completed early on each leg without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a late selection of the TAKEOFF flap setting on the downwind, did not adjust the pitch and power for the configuration change and did not maintain the pattern altitude, descending 380 feet low with the airspeed below 120 KIAS. The base turn was then flown at 50 degrees of bank, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls and directed the go around. The required checks on the downwind remained incomplete.

SP completed the flaps T/O overhead pattern within the desired standards, with break altitude at the 300 feet deviation limit, downwind airspeed 20 knots above the pattern airspeed and final altitude 200 feet high. The TAKEOFF flap selection and two standardized reports were made only after the IP's verbal indications, and the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent sequencing of the T/O flap configuration with the pattern parameters is expected in the following sorties.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern without any verbal prompting from the IP, executing the break within the break zone after clearing the downwind and selecting the TAKEOFF flap setting within its limitation airspeed. Break altitude deviated 230 feet with 12 degrees of bank error and final altitude reached 160 feet high with the airspeed 14 knots fast. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern accurately and promptly, containing break and downwind altitude within 135 feet, break bank within 9 degrees and the downwind and base leg airspeed within 9 knots above the pattern values. The base leg was planned to the Roll Out Point described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, so that the final was flown within 95 feet high and 45 feet low without deviating or converging. The required checks were performed within the gear and flap limitations and the standardized reports were given at the correct points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern with exceptional precision, holding the pattern altitude within 40 feet, the break bank within 3 degrees and the T/O flap pattern airspeeds within 3 knots on every leg. The configuration change was anticipated so that no pitch or power correction was visible on the downwind, and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline 1 NM prior to the threshold. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed without any prompting and no onset of stall characteristics occurred. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a lapse in which a briefed item was omitted under workload, did not perform the required checks on the downwind and did not confirm the landing gear position before the base leg. Downwind altitude was allowed to deviate 340 feet and the airspeed to decay below 120 KIAS, with the result that the IP directed the checks and executed the correction to the pattern altitude. The omission was not detected by the SP at any point in the pattern.

SP, due to an incorrect pitch technique at the T/O flap selection, did not maintain the downwind altitude and airspeed, reaching the 300 feet and 20 knots limits of the criteria before the base turn. The final was flown 200 feet high with the alignment with the RWY centerline completed only at the 1/2 NM point. The deviations were corrected after the IP's verbal indications and the recognition was delayed on both legs.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern within the desired standards, with break altitude deviations of 270 feet, downwind airspeed 18 knots above the pattern airspeed and final altitude 175 feet high. The deviations were recognized and corrected without the IP's intervention, but the T/O flap selection was made late on two patterns and each final required a repeated power correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier sequencing of the configuration change on the downwind is expected to reduce these corrections.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern accurately and promptly, breaking within the break zone with ATC clearance and after clearing the downwind, with break altitude within 115 feet and bank within 7 degrees. The TAKEOFF flap setting was selected within its limitation airspeed, the downwind airspeed was held within 8 knots above the pattern value and never below 120 KIAS, and final altitude was held within 90 feet high and 40 feet low. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed at the correct points with no deviation or convergence from the final. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with pattern altitude deviations of 30 feet, break bank deviations of 2 degrees and the T/O flap airspeeds held within 3 knots on the downwind, base leg and final. The base leg was flown so that the roll out occurred on the RWY centerline without any subsequent correction, and the required checks were completed before each leg. The standardized reports were given in full and on time and the gear and flap limitations were respected throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect break technique with the T/O flap pattern airspeeds, did not execute the break within the break zone and exceeded the break altitude by 400 feet with 20 degrees of bank error. The downwind was entered with the configuration incomplete and the airspeed below 120 KIAS, with the result that the IP directed the flap and gear selections and executed the correction to the pattern altitude. The SP did not recognize the airspeed decay before the IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not maintain the final airspeed and altitude with the T/O flap setting, reaching the 15 knots and 200 feet high limits of the criteria. The A/C converged on the RWY centerline and was aligned only at the 1/2 NM point, and the corrections were applied after the IP's verbal indications. The pattern was completed without the IP touching the controls, but the recognition of both deviations was delayed.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, did not cross-check the altitude and airspeed after the T/O flap selection and allowed the downwind to deviate 230 feet with the airspeed 16 knots above the pattern value. The final was reached 170 feet high and required two power corrections to regain the profile. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern within the desired standards, holding break and downwind altitude within 145 feet, break bank within 10 degrees and the final airspeed within 10 knots above the pattern value. The parameters were accurate and the configuration was managed within its limitations, but on one of the three patterns the final was reached at the outer edge of the altitude criteria and required a late correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the base leg planning with the T/O flap setting is expected to improve.

SP flew the flaps T/O overhead pattern with exceptional precision, with altitude deviations not exceeding 40 feet at the break, on the downwind and on the final and with the T/O flap airspeeds held within 3 knots. Every pattern was flown to the same geometry, with the roll out on the RWY centerline 1 NM prior to the threshold and with no deviation or convergence thereafter. The configuration change, the required checks and the standardized reports were completed without any prompting and within all the gear and flap limitations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern to the desired standard for this Training Section, with the IP directing the airspeed reduction on the downwind and calling the AOA corrections. AOA deviated by up to 3.8 units on the base leg and by 3.4 units on final, with the IP executing part of the turn to final. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent control of the on speed AOA through the downwind, base leg and final is expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP flew the complete AOA overhead pattern without the IP directing or executing any part of it, requiring verbal indications for the airspeed reduction on the downwind and for the AOA corrections on the base leg. AOA was contained at the 3 unit limit on the downwind and on final, with the pattern altitude at the 300 feet deviation limit. The corrections were applied after the IP's indications and the recognition of the AOA excursions was delayed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern without any prompting from the IP, reducing the airspeed accordingly on the downwind and flying the base leg and final on the AOA indication. AOA excursions reached 2.4 units on the base leg and 2 units on final, with final altitude 150 feet high. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern accurately and promptly, holding the AOA within 1.4 units on the downwind, base leg and final and reducing the airspeed accordingly at the correct point. Pattern altitude was contained within 130 feet, the base leg was flown at 40 degrees of bank to the planned Roll Out Point and final altitude was held within 90 feet high and 40 feet low. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed and no onset of stall characteristics occurred. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern with exceptional precision, holding the on speed AOA within 0.3 units throughout the downwind, base leg and final with pattern altitude deviations of 35 feet. The airspeed reduction was anticipated so that the AOA indication was established before the base turn and required no further correction, and the final was flown without deviation or convergence. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect trim and power technique after the airspeed reduction, did not fly the pattern on the AOA indication, allowing excursions of 4.2 units on the base leg and letting the airspeed decay below 120 KIAS on the downwind. The onset of stall characteristics appeared in the base turn, with the result that the IP took the controls and directed the go around. The AOA excursion was not recognized by the SP before the intervention.

SP completed the AOA overhead pattern within the desired standards, with AOA at the 3 unit deviation limit on the base leg and on final and with the pattern altitude at the 300 feet limit. The airspeed reduction and two AOA corrections were made only after the IP's verbal indications and the recognition of the excursions was delayed. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier self-recognition of the AOA trend before the base turn is expected in the following sorties.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern without any verbal prompting from the IP, reducing the airspeed accordingly and giving all the standardized reports. AOA excursions reached 2.2 units on the base leg and 1.8 units on final, with the pattern altitude deviating 230 feet and the final 150 feet high. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern accurately and promptly, holding the AOA within 1.3 units on the downwind, base leg and final and containing the pattern altitude within 135 feet. The base leg was flown at 42 degrees of bank to the Roll Out Point described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the final was held within 95 feet high and 45 feet low without deviating or converging. The required checks were performed within the gear and flap limitations and the standardized reports were given at the correct points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern with exceptional precision, holding the on speed AOA within 0.3 units on every leg and the pattern altitude within 40 feet. The A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline 1 NM prior to the threshold and the final was flown on the AOA indication without deviation or convergence and with no onset of stall characteristics. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed early on each leg without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not cross-check the AOA indication against the airspeed after the landing gear and flaps were selected, allowing an excursion of 4 units on the base leg. The A/C reached the final 320 feet high and below 120 KIAS, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls and directed the go around. The required checks were completed only after the IP called them.

SP, due to a late airspeed reduction on the downwind, did not establish the on speed AOA before the base turn, reaching the 3 unit deviation limit on the base leg and on final. Pattern altitude deviated to the 300 feet limit and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline only at the 1/2 NM point. The corrections were applied after the IP's verbal indications, with delayed recognition of the AOA trend.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern within the desired standards, with AOA excursions of 2.5 units on the base leg, 2 units on final and pattern altitude deviations of 260 feet. The excursions were recognized and corrected without the IP's intervention, but the AOA required repeated corrections on each leg and the Roll Out Point had to be adjusted twice. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more consistent trim and power technique for the on speed AOA is expected to reduce these corrections.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern accurately and promptly, reducing the airspeed accordingly on the downwind and holding the AOA within 1.4 units through the base leg and final. Pattern altitude was contained within 125 feet, final altitude within 90 feet high and 40 feet low, and the A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline before the 1/2 NM point. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed within the gear and flap limitations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the AOA overhead pattern with exceptional precision, holding the on speed AOA within 0.2 units and the pattern altitude within 30 feet from the break to the RWY threshold. The base leg was planned so that the roll out occurred on the RWY centerline with the AOA already established, and no correction was required on final. The required checks and the standardized reports were completed in full and on time and no onset of stall characteristics occurred. Above end of block MIF achieved.
